record.paper_title: Problems and Conjectures Presented at the Third International Conference on Permutation Patterns (University of Florida, March 7-11, 2005)
record.original_question: Let B be a finite set of permutation patterns, let Av(B) be the class of permutations that avoid every pattern in B, and let s_n(B) be the number of permutations of length n in Av(B). A sequence is called P-recursive if it satisfies a linear recurrence with polynomial coefficients. Is the Noonan-Zeilberger conjecture false, and in particular is the sequence s_n(1324) not P-recursive?

evidence.quote: For a set of permutations B define Av(B) to be the set of permutations that avoid all of the permutations in B and let sn(B) denote the number of permutations of length n in Av(B).
A sequence sn is said to be P-recursive (which is short for polynomially recursive) if there are polynomials p0, p1, . . . pk so that pk(n)sn+k + pk−1(n)sn+k−1 + . . . + p0(n)sn = 0.
Conjecture (Doron Zeilberger): The Noonan-Zeilberger Conjecture is false, and, in particular, the sequence sn(1324) is not P-recursive.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set B of permutation patterns, let Av(B) denote the class of permutations that avoid every pattern in B (i.e., contain no subsequence order-isomorphic to any element of B), and let s_n(B) denote the number of permutations of {1,2,...,n} in Av(B). A sequence (a_n)_{n≥0} of integers is called P-recursive (polynomially recursive) if there exist a positive integer k and polynomials p_0(x), p_1(x), ..., p_k(x), with p_k not identically zero, such that
    p_k(n) a_{n+k} + p_{k-1}(n) a_{n+k-1} + ... + p_0(n) a_n = 0
for all sufficiently large n. The Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture asserts that for every finite set B of permutation patterns, the sequence s_n(B) is P-recursive.

Prove or disprove: the sequence s_n(1324), counting permutations of length n that avoid the pattern 1324, is not P-recursive (and hence the Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture is false in this specific case).
artifact.status_search_result: The status of s_n(1324) itself remains open: it is still unknown whether the sequence counting 1324-avoiding permutations is P-recursive. However, the broader Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture has been disproved by Garrabrant and Pak ("Pattern Avoidance is Not P-Recursive"), who exhibited a finite set of patterns whose avoidance counting sequence is not P-recursive. The specific case of 1324 conjectured by Zeilberger is therefore partially resolved (the overarching conjecture is false, but the 1324 question itself is unresolved).

status_evidence.title: Pattern Avoidance is Not P-Recursive
status_evidence.snippet: Garrabrant and Pak construct a finite set of patterns whose avoidance sequence is not P-recursive, disproving the Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The general Noonan–Zeilberger conjecture is false.

status_evidence.title: Noonan-Zeilberger's Conjecture – Igor Pak's blog
status_evidence.snippet: It remains unresolved whether the sequence counting 1324-avoiding permutations is P-recursive.
status_evidence.claim: The specific case s_n(1324) is still open.

status_evidence.title: Staircases, dominoes, and the growth rate of 1324-avoiders
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the growth rate of 1324-avoiding permutations have been studied, but the P-recursiveness question is not settled.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results on the asymptotics of s_n(1324) are known.
